audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Singed levels 2 and 3 and called 4-5 and 6 even, contradicting five of its own whys: whys[0] 'concede the level-1 auto trades entirely', whys[1] 'use Fling to escape, not to kill', whys[2] 'trade even', whys[3] 'banking the gold advantage you need', whys[4] 'he takes more than he gets back'.
audit.why: Volibear's Frenzied Maul is a 5s heal on a champion who out-autos Singed at 1 and 2; the lane only turns once Ghost and the proxy pattern exist at 4-5, and Insanity Potion's Grievous Wounds settles level 6 in Singed's favour. The packet chart reads Volibear / Volibear / Skill / Singed / Singed / Singed / Singed, which is exactly what the prose describes.
audit.corrected: Chart flipped as one group: win[0] and win[1] to Volibear, win[2] to Skill, win[3] and win[4] to Singed, with the matching phases sides.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns on the page; breakdown.cooldowns was template filler.
audit.why: Thundering Smash is 12s at rank 1, Frenzied Maul a flat 5s, Sky Splitter a flat 16s, Stormbringer 160/135/110s. Stormbringer at 160s against Insanity Potion's flat 100s is the concrete reason you can force a second fight he cannot answer, and Frenzied Maul at 5s means his healing is continuous, not a window.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, mid and phases[1].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five strings call Thundering Smash a dash — 'Thundering Smash dash', 'he dashes', 'he has the dash to close', 'dash-into-W-bite burst', 'his tankiness and dash'.
audit.why: Riot: 'Volibear gains speed towards enemies, Stunning and damaging the first one he Attacks.' It is bonus movement speed, not a dash, and the kit carries no dash flag on Q. This changes the counterplay completely: Mega Adhesive's grounding does nothing to it, but Mega Adhesive's slow does, because the whole ability is movement speed. It is also an auto-attack reset — the stun lands on his next Attack, so the wind-up is the tell, not the cast. The page named the wrong ability class and therefore pointed at the wrong half of your W.
audit.corrected: All five restated; the glue's slow, not its grounding, named as the answer to Thundering Smash.

audit.whatIsWrong: Stormbringer being a dash — the one ability of his that grounding actually stops — was never mentioned, and Sky Splitter does not appear on the page at all.
audit.why: Stormbringer is flagged dash, 'mobility that grounding and walls can deny', so Mega Adhesive under him denies the leap and the tower disable that comes with it. Sky Splitter is a 1200-range slow that also shields him if he stands in his own blast, on a flat 16s — that shield is what eats your commit, and 'run through him' advice never accounted for it.
audit.corrected: Grounding-vs-Stormbringer written into late, dosFull[2] and breakdown.cooldowns; Sky Splitter's shield written into whys[2] and spikes[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4] and mid credit Insanity Potion's armour and magic resist for beating Frenzied Maul's healing. The actual mechanism — Grievous Wounds — is never named anywhere in the matchup.
audit.why: Insanity Potion makes Poison Trail apply Grievous Wounds, and Frenzied Maul's second cast on a marked target 'deals bonus damage and Heals Volibear' on a 5s cooldown. Cutting that heal is the whole level-6 swing; resistances are secondary.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds named in whys[4], spikes[1], mid and dontsFull[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing warns that armour alone reads his damage wrong.
audit.why: Frenzied Maul applies on-hit effects and The Relentless Storm stacks attack speed until his attacks deal bonus magic damage — so his output scales with attack speed and includes magic damage. Armour alone is the wrong purchase.

edits.after: The proxy window: Ghost outruns Thundering Smash because it is move speed, not a dash. Bank gold and give him no contact at all.

edits.after: Insanity Potion puts Grievous Wounds on your poison and cuts Frenzied Maul's heal — this is the level where running at him starts paying.

edits.after: Thundering Smash is bonus move speed into a stun on his next attack, and Frenzied Maul heals it all back — concede the level-1 auto trades entirely and just farm.

edits.after: Full kit online and trades stay even: Sky Splitter shields him if he stands in his blast, so Mega Adhesive into Fling punishes overextension, not a kill.

edits.before: Insanity Potion's armor and magic resist outpace his W bite healing; run through him with Poison Trail and he takes more than he gets back.
edits.after: Insanity Potion puts Grievous Wounds on Poison Trail, so Frenzied Maul stops healing him back — run through him and he takes far more than he recovers.

edits.before: Volibear's Thundering Smash dash and W bite give him a reliable kill threat before your Fling-glue combo is fully online — respect the dash.
edits.after: Thundering Smash is move speed into a stun on his next attack, and Frenzied Maul heals the trade back — glue slows the charge, it does not ground it.

edits.before: Insanity Potion's stat dump makes you suddenly tanky enough to run through his claws and trade profitably — he can no longer brute-force you out.
edits.after: Insanity Potion's Grievous Wounds shuts off Frenzied Maul's healing and the stat dump absorbs his claws — he can no longer brute-force you out of lane.

edits.before: Volibear's Thundering Smash is the entire early threat — he dashes, bites with W to heal, and the burst is enough to chunk you before Insanity Potion makes you resilient. At level 1 do not run into melee range to set up Poison Trail; stand back and last-hit, because he wins any auto-trade at this stage cleanly. At level 2 Fling comes online but he has the dash to close regardless, so use the Fling defensively: get him in the air and run rather than looking for a kill. Your job levels 1-3 is to not hand him a free kill while you farm enough gold to proxy.
edits.after: Thundering Smash is the entire early threat — it is bonus move speed toward you, not a dash, and the stun lands on his next attack, so the wind-up is your cue to walk. Frenzied Maul then heals the trade back every 5 seconds. At level 1 do not step into melee to lay Poison Trail; stand back and last-hit, because he wins any auto-trade cleanly. At level 2 Fling exists but he closes anyway, so use it defensively: put him in the air and run rather than hunting a kill. Your job at levels 1-3 is to hand him nothing while you farm the gold to proxy.

edits.before: The matchup flips once you have Ghost and your full kit at level 4. Begin proxying behind his wave — Volibear has no reliable way to catch you if you Ghost out, and every wave you tax costs him CS and forces a decision. At level 6 Insanity Potion is your green light: the armor, magic resist, and health regeneration mean his W bite no longer out-sustains your poison, and you can run through him with Poison Trail active long enough to force him off the wave. Bait Thundering Smash with Ghost, let him miss, then Fling him into your poison cloud for a clean trade. Never commit without tracking Thundering Smash — if he has it up and you are below half health, reset.
edits.after: The matchup flips once you have Ghost and your full kit at level 4. Begin proxying behind his wave — Thundering Smash is move speed rather than a dash, so Ghost simply outruns it, and every wave you tax costs him CS. At level 6 Insanity Potion is your green light: it puts Grievous Wounds on Poison Trail, so Frenzied Maul's 5-second heal stops paying him back and you can run through him long enough to push him off the wave. Bait the charge with Ghost, let the stun whiff, then glue him — the slow is what beats a move-speed charge — and Fling him into the cloud. Never commit while Thundering Smash is up and you are below half health.

edits.before: With Rylai's Crystal Scepter completed the lane is functionally over as a fair contest — every Poison Trail tick slows Volibear, he cannot walk out of the cloud to heal safely with W, and your chase speed with Ghost and passive movement-speed stacking outpaces any repositioning he tries. Split-push the side-lane constantly and make him answer 1v1 on your terms, not in a teamfight where his R tower-disable and dive tool are at full value. His R is your main concern in the two-items phase: if he pops the turret to dive you, treat it as a zone tool and immediately proxy the opposite side rather than fighting under a disabled tower. Force map resources, never his preferred brawl.
edits.after: With Rylai's Crystal Scepter completed the lane is functionally over as a fair contest — every Poison Trail tick slows Volibear, he cannot walk out of the cloud to heal safely with Frenzied Maul, and your chase speed with Ghost and Noxious Slipstream outpaces any repositioning he tries. Split-push the side-lane constantly and make him answer 1v1 on your terms. Stormbringer is your one real concern in the two-item phase, and it is the one ability grounding does stop: it is a leap, so Mega Adhesive under his feet denies the jump and the tower disable that comes with it. At 160s at rank 1 against your flat 100s, you also get your ultimate back first — force map resources, never his brawl.

notes: packet suspectNames for volibear (Insanity Potion, Poison Trail, Thundering Smash) are all false positives. Level-chart flip proposed as one atomic group of five rows. The largest correction is that Thundering Smash is NOT a dash — Riot's text is 'gains speed towards enemies' and the kit carries no dash flag on Q — which means Mega Adhesive's grounding does nothing to it while the slow does; the only groundable ability Volibear has is Stormbringer.
